title: Gouache mixes with water like watercolor, but covers the paper in flat, solid color
alt: Tubes of gouache paint fanned out around a white mixing palette with dabs of colour and three brushes.

posts.facebook:
Imagine watercolor that hides the paper instead of letting it show through. That's gouache.

Like watercolor, gouache paint mixes with water. Unlike watercolor, it's opaque, so it covers the paper in flat, matte color. Tate, the UK's national art museums, notes that it's often used to add highlights to watercolors.

To start, you need only a small set of tubes in the primary colors plus white, two or three round brushes, a palette and some paper. Beginners' courses run at adult education centers and art schools in the UK and the US.

Have you ever painted with gouache?
